I found one bug in the uncommitted `clinic/evaluate.py`, at line 15. I didn't run the code.

The cross-validation splits by visit instead of by patient. `StratifiedKFold` splits rows, but `clinic/data.py` says patients have several visits. Per-patient features like `age` and `n_chronic` repeat across those visits. So one patient's visits can land in both the training and test folds. The model can then recognise patients it has already seen, and the reported PR-AUC will be too high compared with new patients.

The fix is to use `StratifiedGroupKFold` with the patient ID as the group. That means passing `groups=df["patient_id"]` to `cv.split`. `GroupKFold` would also work, but it doesn't stratify.

findings.short_summary: Row-level CV leaks patients across train/test folds
findings.summary: StratifiedKFold splits at the visit level, but data.py says patients have many visits with repeated per-patient features (age, n_chronic), so the same patient lands in both train and test folds.
findings.failure_scenario: A patient's visits are split between train and test. The gradient boosting model memorizes the patient's repeating features (age, n_chronic) and their labels, so test visits are scored on patients it has already seen. The reported PR-AUC is optimistically inflated and won't hold for new patients. Fix: use StratifiedGroupKFold (or GroupKFold) with groups=df['patient_id'] and pass groups to cv.split.
